finding: Indian Electricity Rules 1956, Rule 54 (text read via Indian Kanoon): LV/MV supply voltage may not vary by more than 6 % from the declared voltage; HV +6/-9 %; EHV +10/-12.5 %. Rule 54 applies at the point where supply commences to the consumer; the model applies the band at every feeder node (conservative). Not checked: whether Rule 54 has been superseded or restated in the CEA safety/supply regulations, and the state-commission supply-code limits that actually bind a DISCOM.
action: Keep as design band; cite as 'consistent with +/-6 % in IE Rule 54'; confirm current instrument + state supply code before claiming compliance.

finding: IS 1180 (Part 1):2014 presentation (ITMA) gives distribution-transformer secondary rated voltage as 433 V, 3-phase (250 V single-phase) at no load. The model uses 415 V nominal at the load side, which is the usual declared LV voltage; the 433 V no-load rating is not modelled (no tap/no-load rise).
action: State that tap setting / no-load voltage rise is not modelled.

finding: 250 kVA is a standard IS 1180 (Part 1):2014 three-phase rating (list 6.3...2500 kVA, read in the same source). The source states %impedance values are 'recommended values' but the figure for 250 kVA was not extracted; vector group (Dyn11) not confirmed in the text read. 4.5 % and 1 % load loss remain assumptions.
action: Check IS 1180 Part 1 table for %Z and load-loss at 250 kVA and the vector group before quoting.

item: PV inverter volt-watt curve (v1 1.06, v2 1.10, p2 0.20)
finding: The curve is an IEEE 1547-2018-style placeholder. Could not retrieve IEEE 1547 numeric defaults from an accessible primary source this session (one US utility document read states volt-watt is OFF by default). The CEA draft 'Technical Standards for Connectivity to the Grid' Regulations, 2026 apply only at 33 kV and above (so not to LV rooftop PV); a 2018 CEA draft amendment for DG below 33 kV, as summarised by Mercom, covers protection, harmonics and DC injection and no volt-watt/volt-var requirement was found in what was read.
action: Keep labelled 'prototype assumption (IEEE 1547-style)'. Do NOT call it an Indian requirement.

item: Cable / conductor / neutral parameters (r1 0.32, x1 0.08 ohm/km; neutral 0.64; ampacity 200 A phase, 100 A neutral)
finding: Generic LV four-wire placeholders; not matched to a specific IS cable datasheet (e.g. LT AB cable / XLPE). Neutral sized at half phase ampacity is a deliberate stress assumption.
action: Replace with datasheet values; the assumption-sensitivity study varies impedance and neutral parameters.

finding: No protection coordination, fault-level or earthing study is performed; only steady-state voltage/current/loading limits are monitored.
Per-phase voltages are reported; no unbalance factor limit, THD or flicker assessment.

Value and source (CEA CO2 Baseline Database for the Indian Power Sector V21.0, FY 2024-25) are as stated in the submission; not re-fetched in this session. Grid-average factor applied to the change in net import after losses; a marginal factor would give a different result.
action: Configurable in final/economics.py; re-verify against the database before final claims.

item: All cost inputs (battery, converter, switches, comms, installation, transformer upgrade, second-life)
finding: Placeholders chosen to exercise the cost model (INR). They are not quotes or sourced market prices.
action: Replace with vendor quotes / tariff orders; report cost as scenario, not result.

item: Battery parameters (95 % each way, SoC 10-95 %, 100 kWh / 50 kW)
finding: Prototype assumptions; the battery-size and power sweeps treat size as an output.
Synthetic, seeded; no measured feeder or irradiance data used in the reference experiments. CSV / NASA POWER input modes are provided but only validated on synthetic and user-supplied data.
action: State 'simulation results on synthetic profiles' everywhere.

finding: Synthetic AR(1) error model (sigma PV 15 %, demand 8 %, rho 0.9); metrics describe the error model, not a real forecaster.
